items.title: Is The AI Capex Surge A Threat To Amazon Stock?
items.summary: Amazon.com (AMZN) plans to spend roughly $220 billion of cash on capital in 2026, against $775.7 billion of revenue over the trailing twelve months. The sheer size of that bill introduces notable capital allocation and cash flow pressures that investors must weigh. The rest is who sets the number, and how long the money has to stay out before any of it comes back.

items.title: Google Is Buying Half a Nuclear Plant’s Output Through 2049. Cheap Power Just Became the Real AI Moat.
items.summary: Google just signed a nuclear power contract stretching to 2049, turning electricity from a volatile expense into a fixed cost across two decades of AI growth. Whether that move reshapes Alphabet's competitive position or arrives too late to matter is the real question.

items.title: Is IBM Stock A Buy After Missing On Transaction Processing?
items.summary: International Business Machines (IBM) has given back 12.9% over the past three months and sits at $239.94, about 73% of its 52-week high. Management sees no evidence of clients moving off the mainframe. What has changed is that a key slice of IBM’s transactional software revenue rides on a purchase those clients have learned they can postpone.

items.title: Should You Buy Meta Stock For Cash Flow It Plans To Spend?
items.summary: Meta Platforms (META) trades at about $653, roughly 16% below its 52-week high, and at 11.3 times operating cash flow against 15.2 for the S&P 500. A discount of this scale on a business delivering 28% top-line growth presents a notable valuation divergence, though one largely explained by the company's surging capital commitments. The cash flow that multiple is priced on is money Meta plans to spend.
